*sets down reports with the weariness of one who has seen too many disasters born of carelessness*

The architecture serves the Imperium. I serve the architecture. And this code... would bring the Imperium to its knees.

## Critical Issues

**SQL Injection (Lines 101, 116-118, 128, 151, 175, 193, 207-209)**
Every `fmt.Sprintf` building SQL queries is an open gate for attackers. `GetOrder`, `GetUserOrders`, `ExportOrders`, `ProcessRefund` - they could extract your entire database, including those credit cards you're storing in plain text.

**Plain Text Credit Card Storage (Lines 82, 193)**
You're storing `credit_card` directly in the database. This violates PCI-DSS. You will be fined into oblivion. Being Emperor means everyone lies to you - except the auditors.

## High Severity

**No Error Handling on HTTP Calls (Lines 52, 60-64, 74-77, 133-134, 144-148, 183-185)**
Every `http.Get` and `http.Post` ignores errors. Payment fails silently? Inventory reservation fails? You charge money, lose inventory, save nothing. `resp` could be nil - instant panic.

**Race Condition - Unprotected Cache Access (Lines 89, 95, 113, 137)**
You use `cacheMutex` but never lock it. Concurrent requests will corrupt your cache map and crash your service.

**Fire-and-Forget Goroutines (Lines 67-72, 144-148)**
Inventory reservations run in goroutines with no error handling or synchronization. Order saves successfully while inventory reservation fails silently. You've charged money for items you can't ship.

**Response Body Never Closed (Lines 52, 60-64, 74-77)**
Every HTTP response leaks a connection. Under load, you'll exhaust file descriptors.

## Medium Severity

**Missing Authorization**
No user verification anywhere. Any user can cancel any order, view any order, issue arbitrary refunds.

**Refund Amount Not Validated (Line 183)**
Users can request refunds larger than the order total. Free money.

**Card Masking Crashes on Short Input (Line 218)**
`creditCard[len(creditCard)-4:]` panics if card is fewer than 4 characters.

**No Transaction Boundaries**
Payment charges before database insert. If insert fails, you've charged money for an order that doesn't exist.

## Low Severity

**Unchecked `rows.Next()` Errors (Lines 109, 141, 172, 212)**
**`json.Decode` Errors Ignored (Lines 43, 163, 188)**
**Floating Point for Money (Throughout)** - Use integer cents.

---

*looks toward the window, toward Vorbarr Sultana*

Let it be so. (I hate that phrase.) This code must not merge. It is not that it "works in staging" - it is that your staging environment has not yet been attacked by someone competent. Rewrite with parameterized queries, proper error handling, and for the love of the Imperium, stop storing credit cards.
